blocks.x: Also Bernard(?) Robeson; I was impressed with Bernard(?) Robeson. He had the Beat(?) River Orchestra on WEAF in those years. And I'm still back there, because this is the cradle, you know...!
Well, that's where you were coming from.

He used to come on over the air as the Beat River Orchestra, with (?)Lou Ocillo(?), and William Grant Still was one of the orchestrators for it, and it was composed of trumpet and a chamber music group. And I would say there's a similarity to that music in the... There's a Concerto in F that virtually ...(? )...
So I guess Grant Still probably played in that band, didn't he?

I don't know if he played. I think he wrote for the band more than played. But Bernard(?) Robeson himself was a beautiful orchestrator. They did a... Their work was similar, you know. It was deep spiritual music.

I don't know. I've been trying to track down his music for a good while, and I don't seem to be able to come up with anything. He should be a member of ASCAP, and ASCAP should have the record of his music and (?) publisher. He's documented somewhere. William Grant Still has different publishers. His "Ballad For Americans" written during the Second World War was a bit radical to people, but the lyric, the words... It was written by Biddle, Attorney Biddle, who at that time was under the Roosevelt Administration -- he was the Secretary of State, I think.
